title.en: Volume 61 Biographies 26: Yu Wenshu, Guo Yan

sentences.zh: 宇文述宇文述，字伯通，代郡武川人也。

translations.literal: Yu Wenshu, styled Botong, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenshu, whose courtesy name was Botong, came from Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 本姓破野頭，役屬鮮卑俟豆歸，後從其主為宇文氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was Poyetou; he was in servitude to the Xianbei chief Hudougui, and later followed his lord in taking the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: The family had originally borne the name Poyetou and had been subordinated to the Xianbei leader Hudougui; they later took the surname Yuwen when their lord did.

sentences.zh: 父盛，周上柱國。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was a Superior Pillar of State of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng had held the Zhou rank of Superior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 述少驍銳，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Shu in his youth was fierce and sharp, skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shu was bold and keen, and excelled at archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 年十一時，有相者謂述曰：「公子善自愛，後當位極人臣。

translations.literal: When he was eleven, a physiognomist told Shu: "Young lord, take good care of yourself; hereafter you will rise to the utmost rank among ministers."
translations.idiomatic: At the age of eleven a fortune-teller told him, "Young sir, cherish yourself—you will one day stand at the pinnacle of ministerial power."

sentences.zh: 」周武帝時，以父軍功，起家拜開府。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, by his father's military achievements he first entered service and was appointed Defender-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Wu of Zhou he entered office on his father's military merit and was made Defender-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 述性恭謹沈密，周大塚宰宇文護甚愛之，以本官領護親信。

translations.literal: Shu's nature was respectful, cautious, and reserved; the Great Chancellor of Zhou Yuwen Hu greatly favored him and had him hold his original office while leading Hu's personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was respectful, prudent, and taciturn; Yuwen Hu, the Zhou regent, favored him greatly and kept him in his original post while putting him in charge of Hu's personal entourage.

sentences.zh: 及帝親總萬機，召為左宮伯，累遷英果中大夫，賜爵博陵郡公，尋改封濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally assumed all affairs of state, he was summoned as Left Palatial Steward, was repeatedly promoted to Valiant Fruitful Grand Master, was enfeoffed as Duke of Boling Commandery, and soon had his fief changed to Duke of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor took the reins of government himself, Shu was summoned to serve as Left Palatial Steward, rose through the ranks to Valiant Fruitful Grand Master, was enfeoffed as Duke of Boling, and shortly thereafter had his title changed to Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂相州，述以行軍總管率步騎三千，從韋孝寬擊之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Yu Chi rebelled at Xiangzhou; Shu as Campaigning General-in-Chief led three thousand foot and horse to follow Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wen was still chief minister, Yu Chi rose in rebellion at Xiangzhou; Shu, as campaigning commander, led three thousand infantry and cavalry under Wei Xiaokuan to strike him.

sentences.zh: 軍至河陽，迥遣將李俊攻懷州，述別擊俊軍，破之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Heyang, Chi sent the general Li Jun to attack Huaizhou; Shu separately attacked Jun's army and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Heyang; Chi dispatched Li Jun against Huaizhou, and Shu detached a force, routed Jun's column, and broke it.

sentences.zh: 又與諸將擊尉惇於永橋，述先鋒陷陣，俘馘甚眾。

translations.literal: Again with the various generals he attacked Yu Chi's Yu Dun at Yong Bridge; Shu as vanguard broke the formation, and captives and severed ears were very many.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the other commanders in attacking Chi's lieutenant Yu Dun at Yong Bridge; leading the van, Shu smashed the enemy line and took a great many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 平尉迥，每戰有功，超拜上柱國，進爵褒國公，賜縑三千匹。

translations.literal: When Yu Chi was pacified, in each battle he had merit; he was specially promoted to Superior Pillar of State, advanced in rank to Duke of Baoguo, and granted three thousand bolts of fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign that pacified Chi he distinguished himself in every battle; he was promoted in one step to Superior Pillar of State, raised to Duke of Baoguo, and given three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he was made General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，複以行軍總管率眾三萬，自六合而濟。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, again as Campaigning General-in-Chief he led an army of thirty thousand and crossed from Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen he again served as campaigning commander, leading thirty thousand men across the river from Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 時韓擒、賀若弼兩軍趣丹陽，述進據石頭，以為聲援。

translations.literal: At that time Han Qin and He Ruo's two armies pressed toward Danyang; Shu advanced to hold Stone City as a supporting threat.
translations.idiomatic: While Han Qin and He Ruo were driving on Danyang with two armies, Shu pushed forward and seized Stone City to lend them weight from the flank.

sentences.zh: 陳主既擒，而蕭瓛、蕭岩據東吳之地，擁兵拒守。

translations.literal: After the Chen ruler was captured, Xiao Fan and Xiao Yan held the lands of eastern Wu, gathering troops to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Chen emperor was taken, Xiao Fan and Xiao Yan still held eastern Wu with troops massed for resistance.

sentences.zh: 述領行軍總管元契、張默言等討之，水陸兼進。

translations.literal: Shu leading Campaigning Generals-in-Chief Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and others campaigned against them, advancing by both water and land.
translations.idiomatic: Shu took Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and other campaigning commanders against them in a combined land-and-sea advance.

sentences.zh: 落叢公燕榮以舟師自海至，亦受述節度。

translations.literal: Duke of Luocong Yan Rong came from the sea with a fleet and likewise came under Shu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rong, Duke of Luocong, arrived by sea with a naval force and also placed himself under Shu's orders.

sentences.zh: 上下詔曰：「公鴻勳大業，名高望重，奉國之誠，久所知悉。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict from above, saying: "Sir, your great merit and grand achievement, your high fame and heavy regard, and your loyal service to the state have long been fully known."
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued an edict: "Your great service and far-reaching achievements, your eminence and authority, and your long-proven loyalty to the realm are well known to us."

sentences.zh: 金陵之寇，既已清蕩，而吳會之地，東路為遙，蕭岩、蕭瓛，並在其處。

translations.literal: The bandits of Jinling have already been swept clear, but the lands of Wu and Kuaiji lie far to the east along the eastern route; Xiao Yan and Xiao Fan are both there.
translations.idiomatic: "The enemy at Jinling is already crushed, but Wu and the coastal southeast still lie far down the eastern route, and both Xiao Yan and Xiao Fan are there."

sentences.zh: 公率將戎旅，撫慰彼方，振揚國威，宣佈朝化。

translations.literal: Sir, lead your armed hosts, comfort and reassure that region, raise and display the state's might, and proclaim the court's transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: "Take your armies, pacify that region, display the power of the state, and spread the court's civilizing rule."

sentences.zh: 以公明略，乘勝而往，風行電掃，自當稽服。

translations.literal: With your clear strategy, riding victory to go forth, like wind moving and lightning sweeping, they will naturally submit in prostration.
translations.idiomatic: "With your discernment, pressing the advantage, you will sweep them aside like wind and lightning, and they will surely submit."

sentences.zh: 若使干戈不用，黎庶獲安，方副朕懷，公之力也。

translations.literal: If weapons of war need not be used and the black-haired people obtain peace, that will accord with Our heart—and it will be Sir's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: "If war can be avoided and the people left in peace, that would fulfill Our wishes—and it would be your doing."

sentences.zh: 」陳永新侯陳君范自晉陵奔瓛，並軍合勢。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Yongxin of Chen Chen Junfan fled from Jinling to Fan, and they united their armies and combined their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junfan, Marquis of Yongxin, fled from Jinling to join Fan, and their forces merged.

sentences.zh: 見述軍且至，瓛懼，立柵于晉陵城東，又絕塘道，留兵拒述。

translations.literal: Seeing that Shu's army was about to arrive, Fan was afraid; he set palisades east of Jincheng city and also cut off the pond-road, leaving troops to resist Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan learned that Shu's army was approaching, he grew alarmed, threw up stockades east of Jincheng, severed the canal routes, and left troops to block Shu.

sentences.zh: 瓛自義興入太湖，圖掩述後。

translations.literal: Fan himself entered Tai Lake from Yixing, intending to strike Shu's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Fan himself came from Yixing into Lake Tai, plotting to take Shu from behind.

sentences.zh: 述進破其柵，回兵擊瓛，大敗之，斬瓛司馬曹勒叉。

translations.literal: Shu advanced, broke his palisades, turned his army to strike Fan, greatly defeated him, and beheaded Fan's staff major Cao Lecha.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pushed forward, stormed the stockades, wheeled about to hit Fan, routed him utterly, and killed Fan's staff major Cao Lecha.

sentences.zh: 前軍複陷吳州，瓛以餘眾保包山，燕榮擊破之。

translations.literal: The vanguard again took Wuzhou; Fan with his remaining troops held Mount Bao, and Yan Rong attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard seized Wuzhou again; Fan rallied his remnants on Mount Bao, but Yan Rong broke them there.

sentences.zh: 述進至奉公埭，蕭岩、陳君範等以會稽請降。

translations.literal: Shu advanced to Fenggong Embankment; Xiao Yan, Chen Junfan, and others offered surrender through Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu reached Fenggong Dam, Xiao Yan, Chen Junfan, and others surrendered Kuaiji to him.

sentences.zh: 述許之，二人面縛路左，吳會悉平。

translations.literal: Shu permitted it; the two men bound themselves with faces forward at the left of the road, and Wu and Kuaiji were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shu accepted; the two came forward bound at the roadside, and Wu and the coastal districts were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 以功拜一子開府，賜物三千段，拜安州總管。

translations.literal: For his merit one son was appointed Defender-in-Chief, he was granted three thousand segments of goods, and he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For these deeds one of his sons was made Defender-in-Chief, he received three thousand rolls of goods, and he was appointed military governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 時晉王廣鎮揚州，甚善於述，欲述近己，因奏為壽州刺史總管。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Jin Yang Guang was stationed at Yangzhou and was very friendly with Shu, wishing to have Shu near himself, and so memorialized to have him made Inspector-General of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guang, Prince of Jin, then held Yangzhou and thought highly of Shu; wanting him close at hand, he had him appointed inspector-general of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 王時陰有奪宗之志，請計於述，述曰：「皇太子失愛已久，令德不聞於天下。

translations.literal: The prince at the time secretly harbored the will to seize the succession and asked Shu's counsel; Shu said: "The crown prince has long lost favor; his fine virtue is not heard of throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The prince already harbored designs on the succession and sought Shu's advice. Shu said, "The crown prince has long fallen from grace, and his virtue is scarcely known in the realm."

sentences.zh: 大王仁孝著稱，才能蓋世，數經將領，深有大功。

translations.literal: Your Highness is famed for benevolence and filial piety, your talent surpasses the age, you have repeatedly led armies, and have deep great merit.
translations.idiomatic: "Your Highness is renowned for benevolence and filial duty, your abilities overshadow your peers, you have commanded armies again and again, and your achievements are weighty."

sentences.zh: 主上之與內宮，鹹所鍾愛，四海之望，實歸於大王。

translations.literal: His Majesty and the inner palace all hold you in special love; the hopes of the four seas truly return to Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor and the inner palace both favor you, and the hopes of the empire truly rest with Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 然廢立者，國家之大事，處人父子骨肉之間，誠非易謀也。

translations.literal: Yet removal and establishment are great affairs of state; placed between father and son in flesh and bone, it is truly not an easy scheme.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet to depose and install an heir is a matter of state, and it stands between father and son—hardly a simple plot."

sentences.zh: 然能移主上者，唯楊素耳。

translations.literal: Yet the one who can shift His Majesty's mind is only Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: "Still, the only man who can sway the emperor is Yang Su."

sentences.zh: 素之謀者，唯其弟約。

translations.literal: Among those who counsel Su, there is only his younger brother Yue.
translations.idiomatic: "Of those Su trusts in counsel, only his brother Yue matters."

sentences.zh: 述雅知約，請朝京師，與約相見，共圖廢立。

translations.literal: Shu was on intimate terms with Yue; he asked to go to court at the capital, to meet Yue, and together to plot removal and establishment.
translations.idiomatic: "Shu knows Yue well; let me go to the capital, meet him, and plan the change with him."

sentences.zh: 」晉王大悅，多齎金寶，資述入關。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was greatly pleased and sent much gold and treasure to supply Shu in entering the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was delighted and gave Shu a lavish store of gold and jewels to take into the capital.

sentences.zh: 述數請約，盛陳器玩，與之酣暢，因而共博，每佯不勝，所齎金寶盡輸之。

translations.literal: Shu repeatedly invited Yue, lavishly displayed vessels and curios, drank deeply with him in full enjoyment, and thus gambled together; each time feigning defeat he lost all the gold and treasure he had brought.
translations.idiomatic: Shu called on Yue again and again, displaying fine furnishings and drinking deep with him, then gambling—and always losing on purpose until every treasure he had brought had passed to Yue.

sentences.zh: 約所得既多，稍以謝述。

translations.literal: After Yue's gains were already many, he gradually made his thanks to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue had won a great deal, he began to thank Shu.

sentences.zh: 述因曰：「此晉王之賜，令述與公為歡樂耳。

translations.literal: Shu then said: "This was the Prince of Jin's gift, sent only to have Shu share pleasure with you, Sir."
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "All of this was the Prince of Jin's gift—he meant only that we should enjoy ourselves."

sentences.zh: 」約大驚曰：「何為者？

translations.literal: Yue was greatly startled and said: "What is the purpose?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue was astonished and asked, "What does this mean?"

sentences.zh: 」述因為王申意。

translations.literal: Shu then declared the prince's intent on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Shu then explained the prince's designs.

sentences.zh: 約然其說，退言於素，素亦從之。

translations.literal: Yue approved his reasoning and on returning spoke to Su, and Su likewise followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue accepted the argument, spoke to Su on his return, and Su agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 於是素每與述謀事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su each time took counsel with Shu on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Su and Shu plotted together on every matter.

sentences.zh: 晉王與述情好益密，命述子士及尚南陽公主，前後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin and Shu grew ever closer in affection; he commanded Shu's son Shiji to marry the Princess of Nanyang, and rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The prince drew ever closer to Shu, gave Shu's son Shiji the Princess of Nanyang in marriage, and heaped on them rewards beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 及晉王為皇太子，以述為左衛率。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Shu was made Left Commander of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Shu was made commander of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 舊令，率官第四品，上以述素貴，遂進率品為第三，其見重如此。

translations.literal: By old regulation the commander's office was fourth rank, but the emperor because Shu had long been eminent advanced the commander's rank to third; such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: By statute the guard commander's post was fourth rank, but because Shu had long been prestigious the emperor raised it to third rank—such was the regard he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜左衛大將軍，改封許國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and his fief was changed to Duke of Xu State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne he made Shu General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and changed his title to Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: ，加開府儀同三司，每冬正朝會，輒給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was additionally given the Office of the Same Establishment as the Three Ducal Ministers with an open office, and each year at the winter imperial audience he was given one set of ceremonial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted the privileges of an open office with protocol equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and at each winter court audience he received a full set of ceremonial musicians.

sentences.zh: 從幸榆林，時鐵勒契弊歌棱攻敗吐谷渾，其部攜散，遂遣使請降求救。

translations.literal: Following the emperor on a visit to Yulin, at that time the Tiele chief Qibili Gelen attacked and defeated the Tuyuhun, their tribes scattered in flight, and they sent envoys to request surrender and rescue.
translations.idiomatic: On an imperial tour to Yulin, the Tiele leader Qibili Gelen routed the Tuyuhun and scattered their tribes, and they sent envoys suing for mercy and aid.

sentences.zh: 帝令述以兵屯西平之臨羌城，撫納降附。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shu to station troops at Linqiang city in Xiping, comforting and receiving those who surrendered and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Shu to garrison Linqiang in Xiping and win over the surrendering tribes.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾見述擁強兵，懼不敢降，遂西遁。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun, seeing that Shu held a strong army, were afraid and did not dare to surrender, and so fled west.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun, seeing Shu's strong force, feared to submit and fled westward.

sentences.zh: 述領鷹揚郎將梁元禮、張峻、崔師等追之，至曼頭城，攻拔之，斬三千餘級。

translations.literal: Shu leading Valiant Hawk Captains Liang Yuanli, Zhang Jun, Cui Shi, and others pursued them, reaching Mantou city, stormed and took it, and beheaded more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pursued with the Valiant Hawk captains Liang Yuanli, Zhang Jun, and Cui Shi, seized Mantou city, and killed more than three thousand.

sentences.zh: 乘勝至赤水城，複拔之。

translations.literal: Riding victory he reached Chishui city and again stormed and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory he took Chishui city as well.

sentences.zh: 其餘黨走屯丘尼川，述進擊，大破之，獲其王公、尚書、將軍二百人，前後虜男女四千口而還。

translations.literal: The remaining partisans fled and encamped at Qiuni River; Shu advanced and struck, greatly defeating them, capturing two hundred of their kings, nobles, ministers, and generals, and before and after taking captive four thousand men and women, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant bands fled to the Qiuni River; Shu attacked and smashed them, capturing two hundred princes, ministers, and generals and altogether four thousand men and women before returning.

sentences.zh: 渾主南走雪山，其故地皆空。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun ruler fled south toward Snow Mountain, and his former lands were all emptied.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun king fled south toward Snow Mountain, and his former territories lay empty.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 明年，從帝西幸，巡至金山，登燕支，述每為斥候。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the emperor on a western tour, patrolling to Jinshan, ascending Yanzhi; Shu each time served as scout.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he accompanied the western tour as far as Jinshan and Yanzhi, acting each day as advance scout.

sentences.zh: 時渾賊複寇張掖，進擊走之。

translations.literal: At that time Tuyuhun bandits again raided Zhangye; he advanced, attacked, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raiders struck Zhangye again, he drove them off in a forward attack.

sentences.zh: 還至江都宮，敕述與蘇威常典選舉，參預朝政。

translations.literal: On returning to Jiangdu Palace, an edict ordered Shu together with Su Wei regularly to oversee selection and appointment, participating in court government.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the Jiangdu palace, the emperor charged Shu and Su Wei with routine control of appointments and a share in government.

sentences.zh: 述時貴重，委任與蘇威等，其親愛則過之。

translations.literal: Shu at that time was eminent and weighty; his entrustment was equal to Su Wei and others, but the emperor's personal affection for him surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shu stood then at the height of power, entrusted like Su Wei, but dearer to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝所得遠方貢獻及四時口味，輒見班賜，中使相望於道。

translations.literal: Whatever the emperor received as tribute from distant regions and seasonal delicacies, he would see them distributed in gift to Shu; palace envoys were unceasing on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever rare tribute or seasonal delicacies reached the throne were passed on to Shu, with palace messengers riding in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 述善於供奉，俯仰折旋，容止便辟，宿衛者鹹取則焉。

translations.literal: Shu excelled at attendance and service; in bowing and rising, in turning and wheeling, his bearing and movements were nimble and pleasing, and the palace guards all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had a gift for attendance—every bow and turn, every movement at court—so that even the palace guards took him as their model.

sentences.zh: 又有巧思，凡有所裝飾，皆出人意表。

translations.literal: He also had ingenious conceptions; whatever he furnished or adorned all exceeded men's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: He was inventive too: whatever he designed for display surpassed what others imagined.

sentences.zh: 數以奇服異物進獻宮掖，由是帝彌悅焉。

translations.literal: Repeatedly with strange garments and exotic objects he presented offerings to the inner palace, and by this the emperor grew ever more pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: He often sent rare garments and curios to the inner palace, and the emperor's pleasure in him only deepened.

sentences.zh: 時述貴幸，言無不從，勢傾朝廷。

translations.literal: At that time Shu was favored and eminent; no word of his went unheeded, and his power overawed the court.
translations.idiomatic: In that era Shu's word was law at court, and his power eclipsed every other minister.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍張瑾與述連官，嘗有評議，偶不中意，述張目叱之，瑾惶懼而走，文武百僚莫敢違忤。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Zhang Jin served in connected office with Shu; they once discussed a matter, and it happened not to please him; Shu widened his eyes and shouted at him, and Jin fled in fear and alarm; civil and military officials in their hundreds dared not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin of the Left Guard shared duties with him; once in discussion Shu took offense, glared, and shouted him down until Jin fled in terror—after which no official dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 然性貪鄙，知人有珍異之物，必求取之。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was greedy and base; if he knew someone had a rare or exotic object, he was sure to seek and take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy and base: whenever he heard of some treasure in another's hands, he had to have it.

sentences.zh: 富商大賈及隴右諸胡子弟，述皆接以恩意，呼之為兒。

translations.literal: Great merchants and traders and the sons of the various Hu west of Long, Shu all received with gracious favor and called them "son."
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy merchants and the young men of the western frontier tribes he courted with favor and called "my sons."

sentences.zh: 由是競加饋遺，金寶累積。

translations.literal: Thereupon they vied in adding gifts and presents, and gold and jewels piled up.
translations.idiomatic: They competed to shower him with gifts until gold and gems heaped up around him.

sentences.zh: 後庭曳羅綺者數百，家僮千餘人，皆控良馬，被服金玉。

translations.literal: In his rear courts several hundred trailed silks and brocades; household retainers numbered more than a thousand, all riding fine horses, clad and adorned in gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of women in silk filled his inner quarters; more than a thousand servants rode fine horses and wore gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 述之寵遇，當時莫與為比。

translations.literal: The favor and treatment accorded to Shu at that time had none to compare.
translations.idiomatic: No one at court stood in his shadow.

sentences.zh: 及征高麗，述為扶餘道軍將。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Goguryeo came, Shu was army commander of the Fuyu route.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern campaign he was commander of the Fuyu-route army.

sentences.zh: 臨發，帝謂述曰：「禮，七十者行役以婦人從，公宜以家累自隨。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure the emperor told Shu: "By ritual, one of seventy on campaign may have a wife accompany him; you, Sir, ought to bring your household dependents yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched the emperor told him, "Ritual allows a man of seventy on campaign to take his wife along—you should bring your household."

sentences.zh: 古稱婦人不入軍，謂臨戰時耳。

translations.literal: The ancients said women do not enter the army—that speaks only of the moment of battle.
translations.idiomatic: "When the ancients said women do not enter the army, they meant only in battle."

sentences.zh: 至於營壘之間，無所傷也。

translations.literal: As for within camp and stockade, there is no harm in it.
translations.idiomatic: "In the camps there is no harm in it."

sentences.zh: 項籍虞姬，即其故事。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu's Yu Ji is exactly such a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: "Think of Yu Ji with Xiang Yu—that is the precedent."

sentences.zh: 」述與九軍至鴨綠水，糧盡，議欲班師。

translations.literal: Shu together with the nine armies reached the Yalu River, their grain was exhausted, and they discussed wishing to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shu led nine armies to the Yalu; supplies ran out and the commanders debated withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 諸將多異同，述又不測帝意。

translations.literal: The various generals were mostly divided in opinion, and Shu also could not fathom the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were divided, and Shu could not read the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 會乙支文德來詣其營，述先與于仲文俱奉密旨，令誘執文德。

translations.literal: It happened that Yi Zhongwen came to visit his camp; Shu earlier together with Yu Zhongwen had both received a secret edict ordering them to lure and seize Yi Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi Zhongwen came to his camp, Shu recalled that he and Yu Zhongwen had a secret order to seize him by guile.

sentences.zh: 既而緩縱，文德逃歸，語在《仲文傳》。

translations.literal: Afterward they relaxed and let him go; Yi Zhongwen escaped and returned—as is related in the Biography of Yu Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: They hesitated and let him go; the full account is in the Biography of Yu Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 述內不自安，遂與諸將渡水追之。

translations.literal: Shu inwardly was not at ease and thereupon with the generals crossed the water in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy at heart, Shu crossed the river in pursuit with the other commanders.

sentences.zh: 時文德見述軍中多饑色，欲疲述眾，每鬥便北。

translations.literal: At that time Yi Zhongwen, seeing that Shu's army had many signs of hunger, wished to weary Shu's multitude, and each time they fought he turned north.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Zhongwen, seeing hunger in Shu's ranks, meant to wear them down and gave ground after every clash.

sentences.zh: 述一日之中七戰皆捷，既恃驟勝，又內逼群議，於是遂進，東濟薩水，去平壤城三十裡，因山為營。

translations.literal: Shu in one day fought seven battles and all were victories; relying on sudden victories and inwardly pressed by the crowd of opinions, he thereupon advanced, crossed east over the Sa River, was thirty li from Pyongyang city, and made camp against the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day he won seven engagements; flushed with success and pressed by his officers, he pushed on across the Sa River to within thirty li of Pyongyang and encamped on the hills.

sentences.zh: 文德複遣使偽降，請述曰：「若旋師者，當奉高元朝行在所。

translations.literal: Yi Zhongwen again sent envoys with a false surrender, requesting Shu and saying: "If you withdraw the army, I will present King Gao Yuan at his traveling residence."
translations.idiomatic: Yi Zhongwen sent envoys feigning surrender, promising that if Shu withdrew he would deliver King Gao Yuan at the king's traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 」述見士卒疲敝，不可複戰，又平壤險固，卒難致力，遂因其詐而還。

translations.literal: Shu saw the soldiers weary and worn, unable to fight again; moreover Pyongyang was rugged and firm, hard to exert force against at the end, and so he followed their deception and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his troops exhausted and Pyongyang too strong to storm, he took the feint for truth and turned back.

sentences.zh: 眾半濟，賊擊後軍，於是大潰，不可禁止，九軍敗績，一日一夜，還至鴨綠水，行四百五十裡。

translations.literal: When half the host had crossed, the bandits struck the rear army; thereupon there was a great rout that could not be stopped, the nine armies were defeated, and in one day and one night they returned to the Yalu River, having marched four hundred fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway across the river the enemy hit the rear and the army collapsed beyond control; all nine armies were shattered, and in one day and night they raced four hundred fifty li back to the Yalu.

sentences.zh: 初，渡遼九軍三十萬五千人，及還至遼東城，唯二千七百人。

translations.literal: At first the nine armies crossing the Liao had three hundred five thousand men; when they returned to Liaodong city, there were only two thousand seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The nine armies had crossed the Liao with 305,000 men; at Liaodong only 2,700 remained.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，以述等屬吏。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and handed Shu and the others over to the judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and handed Shu and his peers to the law officers.

sentences.zh: 至東都，除名為民。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Capital his name was struck from the rolls and he became a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern capital he was struck from the registers and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝有事遼東，複述官爵，待之如初。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor had affairs in Liaodong, restored Shu's office and rank, and treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the emperor again turned to Liaodong, Shu's titles were restored and he was treated as before.

sentences.zh: 從至遼東，與將軍楊義臣率兵複臨鴨綠水。

translations.literal: He followed to Liaodong, and with the general Yang Yichen led troops again to approach the Yalu River.
translations.idiomatic: He followed to Liaodong and with Yang Yichen again brought the army to the Yalu.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感作亂，帝召述班師，令馳驛赴河陽，發諸郡兵以討玄感。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Xuangan rebelled; the emperor summoned Shu to withdraw the army and ordered him to ride post-haste by relay to Heyang and mobilize the troops of the various commanderies to attack Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan rose in rebellion; the emperor recalled Shu, sent him galloping by post road to Heyang, and ordered him to raise the commandery armies against Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 時玄感逼東都，聞述軍將至，懼而西遁，將圖關中。

translations.literal: At that time Xuangan was pressing the Eastern Capital; hearing that Shu's army was about to arrive, he was afraid and fled west, intending to seize Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan had been pressing Luoyang; when he heard Shu was coming he fled west toward the passes.

sentences.zh: 述與刑部尚書衛玄、左禦衛將軍來護兒、武衛將軍屈突通等躡之。

translations.literal: Shu together with Minister of Justice Wei Xuan, Left Imperial Guard General Lai Huer, Martial Guard General Qu Tu Tong, and others pursued close upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pursued with Wei Xuan of the Ministry of Justice, Lai Huer of the Left Imperial Guard, Qu Tu Tong of the Martial Guard, and others.

sentences.zh: 至閿鄉皇天原，與玄感相及。

translations.literal: Reaching Huangtian Plain in Wenxiang, they caught up with Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangtian Plain in Wenxiang they overtook Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 述與來護兒列陣當其前，遣屈突通以奇兵擊其後，大破之，遂斬玄感，傳首行在所。

translations.literal: Shu with Lai Huer drew up formation in front of him, sent Qu Tu Tong with a surprise force to strike his rear, greatly defeated him, thereupon beheaded Xuangan, and sent the head to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Lai Huer formed line in front while Qu Tu Tong hit from the rear; they shattered Xuangan's army, cut off his head, and sent it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 賜物數千段。

translations.literal: He was granted several thousand rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He received several thousand rolls of goods as reward.

sentences.zh: 複從東征，至懷遠而還。

translations.literal: Again he followed the eastern campaign, reaching Huaiyuan and returning.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the eastern campaign, advanced as far as Huaiyuan, and then returned.

sentences.zh: 突厥之圍雁門，帝懼，述請潰圍而出。

translations.literal: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, the emperor was afraid; Shu requested breaking out of the encirclement to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, the emperor was terrified; Shu urged breaking out of the encirclement and fleeing.

sentences.zh: 樊子蓋固諫不可，帝乃止。

translations.literal: Fan Zigai firmly remonstrated that it could not be done, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai argued firmly against it, and the emperor abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 及圍解，車駕次太原，議者多勸帝還京師，帝有難色。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, the imperial carriage halted at Taiyuan; many in council urged the emperor to return to the capital, and the emperor showed a troubled expression.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege lifted the court paused at Taiyuan; many advisers urged a return to the capital, and the emperor looked uneasy.

sentences.zh: 述因奏曰：「從官妻子多在東都，便道向洛陽，自潼關而入可也。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon memorialized, saying: "The followers' and officials' wives and children are mostly in the Eastern Capital; by convenient route toward Luoyang, entering through Tong Pass would do."
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized: "Your followers' wives and children are mostly in the eastern capital—take the direct route to Luoyang and enter through Tong Pass."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，至東都，述又觀望帝意，勸幸江都，帝大悅。

translations.literal: That year they reached the Eastern Capital; Shu again watched the emperor's mood and urged a visit to Jiangdu; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: That year they reached Luoyang; reading the emperor's mood, Shu urged a move to Jiangdu, and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 述于江都遇疾，中使相望，帝將親臨視之，群臣苦諫乃止。

translations.literal: Shu fell ill at Jiangdu; palace envoys came one after another; the emperor was about to visit him in person, but the ministers urgently remonstrated and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shu fell ill at Jiangdu; palace messengers shuttled back and forth; the emperor meant to visit him in person until the ministers dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 遂遣司宮魏氏問述曰：「必有不諱，欲何所言？

translations.literal: He then sent the Inner Palace Attendant Lady Wei to ask Shu: "You must have something you dare not speak; what do you wish to say?"
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lady Wei of the Inner Palace to ask Shu: "If you are keeping something back, what is it you wish to say?"

sentences.zh: 」述二子化及、智及，時並得罪於家，述因奏曰：「化及臣之長子，早預籓邸，願陛下哀憐之。

translations.literal: Shu's two sons Huaji and Zhiji were at the time both punished at home; Shu memorialized: "Huaji is my eldest son; he early entered the prince's establishment; I beg Your Majesty to pity him."
translations.idiomatic: Shu's sons Huaji and Zhiji had both been punished at home; he memorialized: "Huaji is my eldest son and entered the prince's household long ago—I beg Your Majesty to show him mercy."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞，泫然曰：「吾不忘也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and said with tears: "I will not forget."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the emperor said through tears, "I will not forget."

sentences.zh: 」及薨，帝為之廢朝，贈司徒、尚書令、十郡太守，班劍四十人，轀輬車，前後部鼓吹，諡曰恭，帝令黃門侍郎裴矩祭乙太牢，鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor suspended court for him, posthumously appointed him Minister of State and Director of the Department of State Affairs and Governor of ten commanderies, granted forty halberd-bearers, an imperial hearse, front and rear ceremonial music, gave the posthumous title Gong, ordered Palace Attendant Pei Ju to sacrifice with a second-grade great offering, and had the Court of Honglu supervise the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu died the emperor canceled court, posthumously made him Minister of State and Director of the Department of State Affairs with nominal authority over ten commanderies, granted forty halberd-bearers, an imperial hearse, and full ceremonial music, gave him the posthumous name Gong, had Pei Ju offer a second-grade sacrifice, and put the Court of Honglu in charge of the funeral.

sentences.zh: 子化及，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Huaji has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaji is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 雲定興雲定興者，附會於述。

translations.literal: Yun Dingxing—Yun Dingxing attached himself to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Dingxing curried favor with Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，定興女為皇太子勇昭訓，及勇廢，除名配少府。

translations.literal: Initially Dingxing's daughter was Bright Instruction to Crown Prince Yong; when Yong was deposed, her name was struck from the rolls and she was assigned to the Palace Supplies Office.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing's daughter had been Bright Instruction to Crown Prince Yong; when Yong was deposed she was struck from the rolls and sent to the Palace Supplies Office.

sentences.zh: 定興先得昭訓明珠絡帳，私賂於述，自是數共交遊。

translations.literal: Dingxing had earlier obtained the Bright Instruction's pearl-net canopy and privately bribed Shu with it; from then on they often associated.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing had earlier obtained the Bright Instruction's pearl-strung canopy and privately bribed Shu with it; thereafter they were often in each other's company.

sentences.zh: 定興每時節必有賂遺，並以音樂幹述。

translations.literal: Dingxing at each season always had gifts, and also used music to please Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At every season Dingxing sent gifts and also used music to win Shu over.

sentences.zh: 述素好著奇服，炫耀時人。

translations.literal: Shu had long loved wearing strange garments, dazzling people of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had long delighted in outlandish dress that dazzled his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 定興為制馬韉，於後角上缺方三寸，以露白色。

translations.literal: Dingxing made a horse saddle for him; at the rear corner a square of three inches was cut away to expose white.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing designed a saddle for him with a three-inch square cut from the rear corner to show white underneath.

sentences.zh: 世輕薄者爭放學之，謂為許公缺勢。

translations.literal: Frivolous men of the age vied to imitate it, calling it Duke Xu's truncated style.
translations.idiomatic: Frivolous men of the day copied it and called the fashion "Duke Xu's gap."

sentences.zh: 又遇天寒，定興曰：「入內宿衛，必當耳冷。

translations.literal: Again when the weather was cold, Dingxing said: "Entering the inner palace for night guard, the ears will surely be cold."
translations.idiomatic: When cold weather came Dingxing said, "On night duty inside the palace your ears are bound to freeze."

sentences.zh: 」述曰：「然。

translations.literal: Shu said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "Quite so."

sentences.zh: 」乃制裌頭巾，令深袙耳。

translations.literal: He then made a layered head-cloth, having it deeply cover the ears.
translations.idiomatic: He had a layered head-wrap made that covered the ears deeply.

sentences.zh: 又學之，名為許公袙勢。

translations.literal: Again they imitated it, calling it Duke Xu's wrapped-ear style.
translations.idiomatic: Others copied that too and called it "Duke Xu's wrap."

sentences.zh: 述大悅曰：「雲兄所作，必能變俗。

translations.literal: Shu was greatly pleased and said: "What Elder Brother Yun has made will surely change custom."
translations.idiomatic: Shu was delighted and said, "Whatever Elder Brother Yun devises is sure to set a new fashion."

sentences.zh: 我聞作事可法，故不虛也。

translations.literal: I have heard that what one does can become a model—thus it is not in vain.
translations.idiomatic: They say useful work becomes a model for others—he is never wasting his effort.

sentences.zh: 」後帝將事四夷，大造兵器，述薦之，因敕少府工匠並取其節度。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor was about to undertake affairs against the four barbarian directions and greatly made weapons, Shu recommended him, and by edict the craftsmen of the Palace Supplies Office all followed his specifications.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later prepared for campaigns on all frontiers and ordered a vast armory, Shu recommended him, and the Palace Supplies craftsmen were ordered to follow his designs.

sentences.zh: 述欲為之求官，謂定興曰：「兄所制器仗併合上心，而不得官者，為長寧兄弟猶未死耳。

translations.literal: Shu wished to seek office for him and said to Dingxing: "The arms and armor you make all suit His Majesty's heart, yet you cannot obtain office because the Changning brothers are still not dead."
translations.idiomatic: Shu wanted an office for him and said, "Your arms and armor please the emperor, yet you cannot rise while the Changning princes still live."

sentences.zh: 」定興曰：「此無用物，何不勸上殺之。

translations.literal: Dingxing said: "These useless fellows—why not urge the emperor to kill them."
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing said, "Those useless men—why not urge the emperor to kill them?"

sentences.zh: 」述因奏曰：「房陵諸子，年並成立。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "The sons at Fangling are all grown to maturity."
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized: "The princes at Fangling are all grown men."

sentences.zh: 今欲動兵征討，若將從駕，則守掌為難；

translations.literal: Now wishing to mobilize armies for campaign, if they follow the carriage, guarding and holding will be difficult;
translations.idiomatic: "If we mobilize for war and they accompany the court, who will guard them?"

sentences.zh: 若留一處，又恐不可。

translations.literal: If left in one place, again we fear it may not do.
translations.idiomatic: "If we leave them in one place, that is no safer."

sentences.zh: 進退無用，請早處分。

translations.literal: Advancing or retreating they are of no use—please dispose of them early.
translations.idiomatic: "They are useless either way—please deal with them soon."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，因鴆殺長寧，又遣以下七弟分配嶺表，仍遣間使于路盡殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; by poison he killed Changning, and sent the seven younger brothers below to be distributed to Lingnan, still sending secret agents on the road to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed: Changning was poisoned, the seven younger brothers were sent to the far south, and agents on the road killed them all.

sentences.zh: 五年，大閱軍實，帝稱甲仗為佳。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, a great review of military stores was held; the emperor praised the armor and weapons as excellent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor held a grand review of the armory and praised the weapons.

sentences.zh: 述奏曰：」並雲定興之功也。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "All are Yun Dingxing's achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized that the credit belonged entirely to Yun Dingxing.

sentences.zh: 」擢授少府丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Assistant Director of the Palace Supplies Office.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing was promoted to assistant director of the Palace Supplies Office.

sentences.zh: 尋代何稠為少監，轉衛尉少卿，遷左禦衛將軍，仍知少府事。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced He Chou as Assistant Superintendent, transferred to Assistant Minister of the Guard, was promoted to Left Imperial Guard General, and still oversaw Palace Supplies affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced He Chou as assistant superintendent, became assistant minister of the guard, rose to Left Imperial Guard general, and still oversaw Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made general-in-chief of the Left Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 凡述所薦達，皆至大官。

translations.literal: All whom Shu recommended and advanced reached high offices.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone Shu recommended rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 趙行樞乙太常樂戶，家財億計，述謂為兄，多受其賄。

translations.literal: Zhao Xingshu, a music-household member of the Grand Music Office, had household wealth reckoned in the hundreds of millions; Shu called him elder brother and received much bribery from him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xingshu of the Grand Music Office—a music-household man worth hundreds of millions—Shu called "elder brother" and took heavy bribes from him.

sentences.zh: 稱其驍勇，起家為折衝郎將。

translations.literal: Praising his fierceness and courage, he entered office as Ironside Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Praising his valor, Shu had him enter service as an Ironside commandant.

sentences.zh: 郭衍郭衍，字彥文，自雲太原介休人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yan, styled Yanwen, claimed descent from Jiexiu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yan, styled Yanwen, claimed Taiyuan's Jiexiu as his ancestral home.

sentences.zh: 父以舍人從魏武帝入關，其後官至侍中。

translations.literal: His father as a palace attendant followed Emperor Wu of Wei in entering the passes; afterward he reached the office of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father had followed Emperor Wu of Wei into the passes as a palace attendant and later rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 衍少驍武，善騎射。

translations.literal: Yan in his youth was fierce in martial arts, skilled at riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yan was martial and excelled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 周陳王純引為左右，累遷大都督。

translations.literal: The Zhou Prince of Chen Chun took him into his personal staff; he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chun of Chen took him into his household, and he rose to grand commander.

sentences.zh: 時齊氏未平，衍奉詔於天水募人，以鎮東境，得樂徙千餘家，屯於陝城。

translations.literal: At that time the Qi state was not yet pacified; Yan received orders at Tianshui to recruit men to secure the eastern border, obtaining more than a thousand relocated households of the Yue people and stationing them at Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: While Qi was still unconquered, Yan was ordered to recruit at Tianshui for the eastern frontier, settled more than a thousand Yue migrant households at Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 拜使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bearer of the staff, general of chariots and cavalry, and equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 每有寇至，輒率所領禦之，一歲數告捷，頗為齊人所憚。

translations.literal: Whenever bandits came he led his command to resist them; several times each year he reported victories, and the Qi people came to fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever raiders appeared he led his men against them; victories were reported many times a year, and the Qi came to fear him.

sentences.zh: 王益親任之。

translations.literal: The prince grew ever more intimate with and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince trusted him ever more deeply.

sentences.zh: 建德中，周武帝出幸雲陽，衍朝於行所，時議欲伐齊，衍請為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the Jiande era, Emperor Wu of Zhou went on tour to Yunyang; Yan attended at the traveling palace; at the time council discussed attacking Qi, and Yan requested to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiande period, when Emperor Wu toured Yunyang, Yan came to the traveling palace; as an attack on Qi was debated, Yan asked to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 攻河陰城，授儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Attacking Heyin city, he was appointed Grand Master with Equal Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Heyin city he was made a grand master with equal protocol.

sentences.zh: 武帝圍晉州，慮齊兵來援，令衍從陳王守千里徑。

translations.literal: When the emperor besieged Jinyang, fearing Qi reinforcements, he ordered Yan to follow the Prince of Chen in guarding the Thousand-Li Path.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Jinyang the emperor, fearing Qi relief, had Yan follow Prince Chen in guarding the Thousand-Li Path.

sentences.zh: 又從武帝與齊主大戰于晉州，追齊師至高壁，敗之。

translations.literal: Again he followed the emperor in the great battle with the Qi ruler at Jinyang, pursued the Qi army to Gaobi, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the emperor in the great battle at Jinyang, pursued the Qi to Gaobi, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 仍從平并州，以功加授開府，封武強縣公，邑一千二百戶，賜姓叱羅氏。

translations.literal: Still following, he pacified Bingzhou; for merit he was additionally appointed Defender-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuqiang with a fief of twelve hundred households, and granted the surname Chiluo.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Bingzhou, was further made Defender-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuqiang with 1,200 households, and given the surname Chiluo.

sentences.zh: ，為右中軍熊渠中大夫。

translations.literal: He was made Bear-Bearon Grand Master of the Right Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became Bear-Bearon grand master of the Right Central Army.

sentences.zh: 尉迥之起逆，從韋孝寬戰于武陟，進戰於相州。

translations.literal: When Yu Chi rose in rebellion, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in battle at Wuzhi and advanced to fight at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chi rebelled he fought under Wei Xiaokuan at Wuzhi and again at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，迥遣弟子勤為青州總管，率青、齊之眾來助迥。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chi had sent his nephew Qin as Commander-in-Chief of Qingzhou, leading the troops of Qing and Qi to aid Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Chi had earlier sent his nephew Qin as military governor of Qingzhou with Qing and Qi troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 迥敗，勤與迥子惇、祐等欲東奔青州。

translations.literal: When Chi was defeated, Qin with Chi's sons Dun and You and others wished to flee east to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chi was beaten, Qin with Chi's sons Dun and You planned to flee east to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 衍將精騎一千追破之，執祐於陣，勤遂遁走，而惇亦逃逸。

translations.literal: Yan led a thousand elite cavalry in pursuit, broke them, and seized You on the field; Qin then fled, and Dun also escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yan pursued with a thousand elite horsemen, broke them, seized You in battle, while Qin and Dun escaped.

sentences.zh: 衍至濟州，入據其城，又擊其餘党於濟北，累戰破之，執送京師。

translations.literal: Yan reached Jizhou, entered and held its city, again struck their remaining partisans in Jibei, repeatedly defeated them in battle, and sent captives to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jizhou, held the city, crushed the remnant bands in Jibei, and sent prisoners to the capital.

sentences.zh: 超授上柱國，封武山郡公。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to Superior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Wushan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in one step to Superior Pillar of State and made Duke of Wushan.

sentences.zh: 賞物七千段。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with seven thousand rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He received seven thousand rolls of goods as reward.

sentences.zh: 密勸高祖殺周室諸王，早行禪代。

translations.literal: He secretly urged Gaozu to kill the kings of the Zhou imperial house and carry out the transfer of the mandate early.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly urged Gaozu to kill the Zhou imperial princes and seize the throne without delay.

sentences.zh: 由是大被親昵。

translations.literal: Thereby he came to be greatly favored and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: From this he won exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: ，敕復舊姓為郭氏。

translations.literal: By edict his former surname was restored to Guo.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his original surname Guo.

sentences.zh: 突厥犯塞，以衍為行軍總管，領兵屯於平涼。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, Yan was made Campaigning General-in-Chief and led troops stationed at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks raided the frontier he was made campaigning commander and garrisoned Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 數歲，虜不入。

translations.literal: For several years the barbarians did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: For several years the nomads did not cross in.

sentences.zh: 征為開漕渠大監。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Superintendent of the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to superintend the Grand Canal project.

sentences.zh: 部率水工，鑿渠引渭水，經大興城北，東至於潼關，漕運四百餘裡。

translations.literal: He directed the water workers, dug a canal to draw the Wei River, passed north of Daxing city, and ran east to Tong Pass—four hundred-odd li of transport.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the diggers to channel the Wei north of Daxing and east to Tong Pass—more than four hundred li of transport.

sentences.zh: 關內賴之，名之曰富民渠。

translations.literal: Within the passes they relied on it, and it was named the Canal for Enriching the People.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong depended on it, and it was named the Canal for Enriching the People.

sentences.zh: 五年，授瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇秋霖大水，其屬縣多漂沒，民皆上高樹，依大家。

translations.literal: Autumn rains brought great floods; many of his subordinate counties were inundated, and the people all climbed tall trees and relied on great houses.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn floods drowned many counties; people climbed trees and clung to great houses.

sentences.zh: 衍親備舩栰，並齎糧拯救之，民多獲濟。

translations.literal: Yan personally prepared boats and rafts and also carried grain to rescue them; many of the people were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Yan himself prepared boats and grain and rescued them; many survived.

sentences.zh: 衍先開倉賑恤，後始聞奏。

translations.literal: Yan first opened the granaries for relief, and only afterward reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the granaries before reporting to court.

sentences.zh: 上大善之，選授朔州總管。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved of this and selected him for appointment as Commander-in-Chief of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this and made him military governor of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 所部有恆安鎮，北接蕃境，常勞轉運。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction was Heng'an Fort, bordering the barbarian lands to the north and constantly burdened by transport.
translations.idiomatic: His district held Heng'an Fort on the northern frontier, where transport was a constant strain.

sentences.zh: 衍乃選沃饒地，置屯田，歲剩粟萬餘石，民免轉輸之勞。

translations.literal: Yan then selected fertile land, established military colonies, and each year had a surplus of more than ten thousand shi of grain; the people were spared the labor of transport.
translations.idiomatic: He chose fertile ground for military colonies and saved more than ten thousand shi yearly, sparing the people transport duty.

sentences.zh: 又築桑乾鎮，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: He also built Sanggan Fort—all met with approval.
translations.idiomatic: He also built Sanggan Fort, and both projects won approval.

sentences.zh: 十年，從晉王廣出鎮揚州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed Prince of Jin Yang Guang in going out to station at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he followed Prince of Jin Yang Guang to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇江表構逆，命衍為總管，領精銳萬人先屯京口。

translations.literal: When rebellion arose in the lower Yangtze region, he was ordered as commander-in-chief to lead ten thousand elite troops first to encamp at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: When the lower Yangtze rebelled he was made commander and led ten thousand elite troops to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 于貴洲南與賊戰，敗之，生擒魁帥，大獲舟楫糧儲，以充軍實，乃討東陽、永嘉、宣城、黟、歙諸洞，盡平之。

translations.literal: South of Gui Prefecture he fought the bandits, defeated them, captured their chieftains alive, greatly obtained boats, oars, grain, and stores to fill the army's needs, and then campaigned against the cave settlements of Dongyang, Yongjia, Xuancheng, Yi, and She, pacifying them all.
translations.idiomatic: South of Gui he defeated the rebels, captured their leaders, seized boats and grain for the army, and pacified the cave settlements of Dongyang, Yongjia, Xuancheng, Yi, and She.

sentences.zh: 授蔣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 衍臨下甚踞，事上奸諂。

translations.literal: Yan toward subordinates was very arrogant; toward superiors he was sycophantic and flattering.
translations.idiomatic: Toward subordinates Yan was overbearing; toward superiors he flattered and fawned.

sentences.zh: 晉王愛昵之，宴賜隆厚。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was fond of and intimate with him; banquets and gifts were generous and thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin favored him with lavish feasts and gifts.

sentences.zh: 遷洪州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 王有奪宗之謀，托衍心腹，遣宇文述以情告之。

translations.literal: The prince had designs on the succession and made Yan his trusted confidant, sending Yuwen Shu to tell him the situation in full.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, plotting for the succession, made Yan his confidant and sent Yuwen Shu to disclose the plan.

sentences.zh: 衍大喜曰：「若所謀事果，自可為皇太子。

translations.literal: Yan was greatly pleased and said: "If the plot succeeds, I can naturally become crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Yan was overjoyed and said, "If the plot succeeds, I could become crown prince myself."

sentences.zh: 如其不諧，亦須據淮海，複梁、陳之舊。

translations.literal: If it does not succeed, we must still hold Huaihai and restore the old domains of Liang and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: "If it fails, we must still hold the Huai-Hai region and restore the old Liang and Chen territories."

sentences.zh: 副君酒客，其如我何？

translations.literal: What can the deputy lord and the wine guest do to us?
translations.idiomatic: "What can the crown prince and that wine-bibbing prince do to us?"

sentences.zh: 」王因召衍，陰共計議。

translations.literal: The prince thereupon summoned Yan and secretly plotted together.
translations.idiomatic: The prince summoned Yan and they plotted in secret.

sentences.zh: 又恐人疑無故來往，托以衍妻患癭，王妃蕭氏有術能療之。

translations.literal: Again fearing that people would suspect their coming and going without cause, they used as a pretext that Yan's wife suffered from goiter and that the princess consort Xiao had a method that could cure it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing suspicion over their constant visits, they claimed Yan's wife had goiter and that Princess Xiao could cure it.

sentences.zh: 以狀奏高祖，高祖聽衍共妻向江都，往來無度。

translations.literal: He memorialized the situation to Gaozu; Gaozu permitted Yan to bring his wife to Jiangdu, and they came and went without limit.
translations.idiomatic: They reported this to Gaozu, who allowed Yan to take his wife to Jiangdu back and forth without restraint.

sentences.zh: 衍又詐稱桂州俚反，王乃奏衍行兵討之。

translations.literal: Yan again falsely reported that the Li of Guizhou had rebelled; the prince then memorialized to send Yan with troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also fabricated a Li rebellion in Guizhou, and the prince memorialized to send him against it.

sentences.zh: 由是大修甲仗，陰養士卒。

translations.literal: Thereby he greatly repaired armor and weapons and secretly nurtured soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he rebuilt arms on a large scale and secretly trained troops.

sentences.zh: 及王入為太子，征授左監門率，轉左宗衛率。

translations.literal: When the prince entered the capital as crown prince, Yan was summoned and appointed Left Commander of the Palace Gate, then transferred to Left Commander of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Yan was summoned as left commander of the palace gate, then of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖于仁壽宮將大漸，太子與楊素矯詔，令衍、宇文述領東宮兵，帖上臺宿衛，門禁並由之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu at Renshou Palace was about to die, the crown prince together with Yang Su forged an edict ordering Yan and Yuwen Shu to lead the Eastern Palace troops, post them to guard the upper terrace, and put gate and guard control entirely in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: As Gaozu lay dying at Renshou Palace, the crown prince and Yang Su forged an edict putting Yan and Yuwen Shu in charge of Eastern Palace troops, palace guards, and all gates.

sentences.zh: 及上崩，漢王起逆，而京師空虛，使衍馳還，總兵居守。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Prince of Han rose in rebellion while the capital was empty; Yan was sent galloping back to gather troops and hold the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died the Prince of Han rebelled with the capital thinly held; Yan was sent racing back to take command of the defense.

sentences.zh: ，拜左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general-in-chief of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，令衍統左軍，改授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Jiangdu, he ordered Yan to command the left army and changed his appointment to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On the tour to Jiangdu the emperor put Yan in command of the left army and promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 又從討吐谷渾，出金山道，納絳二萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Again he followed in the campaign against the Tuyuhun, taking the Jinshan route and receiving more than twenty thousand households of the Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the campaign against the Tuyuhun by the Jinshan route and brought in more than twenty thousand Jiang households.

sentences.zh: 衍能揣上意，阿諛順旨。

translations.literal: Yan could gauge the emperor's intent and flatter by following his wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Yan could read the emperor's mind and flatter him by echoing his wishes.

sentences.zh: 帝每謂人曰：「唯有郭衍，心與朕同。

translations.literal: The emperor often said to people: "Only Guo Yan has a heart the same as Mine."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said, "Only Guo Yan's heart matches mine."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗勸帝取樂，五日一視事，無得效高祖空自劬勞。

translations.literal: He also once urged the emperor to take pleasure, holding audience once every five days, and not imitate Gaozu in toiling in vain.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the emperor to enjoy himself and hold court only every five days rather than wear himself out like Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，益稱其孝順。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and praised his filial obedience all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and praised him all the more for his dutifulness.

sentences.zh: 初，新令行，衍封爵從例除。

translations.literal: Initially, when the new regulations took effect, Yan's enfeoffment was removed according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the new statutes took effect, Yan's enfeoffment was struck according to rule.

sentences.zh: 六年，以恩幸封真定侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, by favor he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending as a favorite.

sentences.zh: 七年，從往江都，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed the emperor to Jiangdu and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed the emperor to Jiangdu and died there.

sentences.zh: 贈左衛大將軍，賵賜甚厚，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Guard; funeral gifts were very generous; his posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general-in-chief of the Left Guard, given lavish funeral gifts, and granted the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 長子臻，武牙郎將。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhen was a Martial Tooth Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhen was a Martial Tooth commandant.

sentences.zh: 次子嗣本，孝昌縣令。

translations.literal: His second son Siben was Magistrate of Xiaochang.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Siben was magistrate of Xiaochang.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：謇謇匪躬，為臣之高節，和而不同，事君之常道。

translations.literal: Commentary. The historiographer says: Earnest self-devotion without sparing the body is the highest integrity of a minister; harmony without sameness is the constant way of serving a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary. The historiographer writes: To devote oneself utterly without sparing the body is a minister's highest integrity; to harmonize without conforming is the constant way of serving a ruler.

sentences.zh: 宇文述、郭衍以水濟水，如脂如韋，便辟足恭，柔顏取悅。

translations.literal: Yu Wenshu and Guo Yan used water to aid water, were like grease and like leather, nimble and obsequious in bearing, soft in countenance to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenshu and Guo Yan poured water on water—supple as grease and leather, quick to bow and scrape, soft-faced to please.

sentences.zh: 君所謂可，亦曰可焉，君所謂不，亦曰不焉。

translations.literal: What the lord called acceptable, they also said was acceptable; what the lord called not, they also said was not.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler said yes, they said yes; when he said no, they said no.

sentences.zh: 無所是非，不能輕重，默默苟容，偷安高位，甘素餐之責，受彼己之譏。

translations.literal: Without any judgment of right and wrong, unable to weigh heavy or light, silently tolerating in complacency, stealing ease in high position, willingly bearing the blame of eating salary without work, receiving the ridicule of others and oneself.
translations.idiomatic: They judged nothing, weighed nothing, mutely endured in high place, ate their salaries in idleness, and earned the scorn of others and of themselves.

sentences.zh: 此固君子所不為，亦丘明之深恥也。

translations.literal: This is what a gentleman will not do, and is also what Qiu Ming deeply shamed.
translations.idiomatic: That is what gentlemen refuse to do—and what Qiu Ming counted a deep disgrace.
